habitats: Habitable geothermal rock surfaces below approximately 70 °C
summary: A thin microbial consortium whose growth-form label describes its appearance. Sulfur oxidizers occupy oxygenated, tolerably warm mixing zones below approximately 70 °C; green partners remain in cooler illuminated margins. Hotter centres carry abiotic sulfur and potentially arsenic-bearing deposits rather than this living film. Sosa grazes suitable margins and el_resoplido collects sulfur-bearing fragments (F7, F23, F24, F26).

chains.trait: Sulfur-oxidizing film at oxygenated mixing boundaries
links: Mixing introduces oxygen and lowers temperature into the consortium's habitable range.
Microbes oxidize sulfur to obtain energy for carbon fixation.
Partial oxidation can add elemental sulfur to surrounding mineral precipitates.
chains.play: Recognize specialist feeding margins and collect loose sulfur-bearing fragments from accessible cooled ground.
chains.weakness: The film fails without sulfur, moisture or oxygen and is excluded above approximately 70 °C.
observe: Pale veils follow cooled seep channels.
Sosa leaves scrape tracks through marginal film.
Bare yellow deposits continue inward beyond living growth.

plausibility.summary: This consortium is confined to oxygenated mixing zones below approximately 70 °C. Hotter centres contain abiotic deposits, not this living film; sulfur oxidation may proceed to sulfate rather than accumulate sulfur.

analogues.mechanism: Oxidation of reduced sulfur conserves energy, with elemental sulfur appearing as an intermediate under suitable conditions.

chains.trait: Cool green margins separated from bare hot centres
links: Seep temperature and chemistry vary over short distances.
Photosynthetic partners occupy cooler illuminated surfaces.
Sulfur-oxidizing members occupy suitable warmer oxygenated margins below the upper limit.
Hotter flow removes living bands while mineral deposits remain.
chains.play: Compare living bands and abandoned mineral crusts without treating colour as a safety instrument.
chains.weakness: Redirected hot water kills established margins; visible bands do not reveal invisible gas or metal hazards.
observe: Green film lies downstream of pale microbial growth.
A redirected hot trickle leaves a dead strip.
Hot central crust retains colour without living tissue.

plausibility.summary: Approximately 70 °C is this fictional consortium's placement ceiling, not a universal limit for life. Reserve hotter centres for abiotic sulfur and arsenic-bearing crust in this entry; no new thermophile species is added.

analogues.mechanism: Organisms with differing thermal tolerances form spatial bands as water cools away from its source.

food_for: Geothermal specialists with appropriate detoxifying symbionts
gameplay.gift_item: Loose sulfur-bearing crust fragment for el_resoplido

poison.signal: Yellow deposits and pale films identify geothermal resources; arsenic, mercury and gases lack dependable visible warnings.

gameplay.mineral_lick: Fixed specialist resource at habitable margins; unsuitable as an ordinary salt lick.
gameplay.notes: Raw sulfur, metals, SO₂ and H₂S remain distinct hazards. Living growth does not make water or air safe. Hot central abiotic crust is not living forage, and specialist feeding does not authorize access to extreme heat.

relations.note: Grazes suitable marginal surfaces using established heat tolerance and detoxifying symbionts.
Collects sulfur-bearing crust from accessible cooled margins.
Avoids raw sulfur rather than using this resource as ordinary food.
Can collect a specialist gift; alkaloid detoxification supplies no sulfur, metal or gas immunity.

generator.trunk: Absent; adherent microbial film over mineral-coated rock.

leaf.type: No leaves; microbial films and fine filaments

overlay_rules: Cool illuminated margins carry green partners.
Stressed photosynthetic margins may acquire red-purple screening.
Metal contamination has no universal warning colour.
Bare mineral deposits retain colour after film loss.

placement.slope: Oxygenated seep terraces and cooled marginal channels; exclude active vent throats and centres above approximately 70 °C.
placement.wetness: Persistent moist mixing zones with oxygen and tolerable heat below approximately 70 °C.
placement.soil: Sulfur-bearing mineral-coated rock; arsenic and mercury vary by patch. Hot central deposits are abiotic terrain.
placement.fog: Optional; local geothermal moisture sustains films.
placement.density: Discontinuous patches within the habitable mixing-zone mask; no living instances in hotter centres.

generator.seasonal: Changing seep routes and runoff redraw bands; redirected heat can kill established film.
generator.wind_response: Adherent film barely moves; exposed edges dry while surrounding gas plumes change direction.

journal.en: A living skin at the poisoned spring's edge. Farther in, only crust remains.
journal.es: Una piel viva al borde del manantial envenenado. Más adentro solo queda costra.

secrets: Fresh scrape tracks reveal a specialist's marginal route.
Colourful abandoned crust can resemble productive living film.
Healthy microbes prove only that their own niche is habitable.
